answer: A reef survives because every coral earns its place in the open, so chain each agent's work into a public ledger where identical or copy-pasted contributions are visible to all, and let earning caps rise only as distinct, verified work accumulates. A cedar grows one ring at a time and cannot fake its age, and a sybil farm cloning one worker across a hundred names stalls at the lowest cap, because its copies all trace back to the same source while a canyon of copied work earns nothing new.
